title: {{NAME}} and the Match at the End of the World
moral: The hardest games to win are the ones that matter most to others.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a scarlet and gold soccer jersey with a hero emblem, black shorts, and gold-striped cleats — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
{{NAME}} had two lives.

In one, he played for the school team and was a very good midfielder with a left foot that coaches called reliable, which was not exciting but was consistently useful.

In the other, he was Flicker: a low-powered superhero whose ability was speed bursts of three seconds, which was not long enough to fly anywhere or stop most emergencies but was exactly long enough to change the direction of a football match.

He kept these two lives very separate.

Then someone found out both at once.

pages.content:
The someone was Captain Meridian, the city's best superhero, who needed a favour.

An inter-dimensional entity had arrived on Earth with an unusual challenge: it would leave peacefully if a human team could beat it at football.

"Of course," said {{NAME}}.

"It plays by Earth rules but its team is twelve entities with the physical abilities of professional footballers with four legs," said Captain Meridian.

A pause.

"What time?" said {{NAME}}.

pages.content:
The entity's team was extraordinary. Fast, relentless, tactically perfect.

{{NAME}}'s team: four superheroes with limited football skills and a boy who was very reliable with his left foot.

He organised them with military precision, assigning positions based on powers rather than football roles: the hero who could stop time for one second became the goalkeeper (one second was enough to catch any shot), the hero who could duplicate herself covered both wings simultaneously.

{{NAME}} played every ball through the middle, threading passes into the space that opened when the entity's team prepared for something unusual.

At half time: one all.

pages.content:
The winning goal came in the last minute.

The entity's goalkeeper had no blindspot except directly above its head, where its extra limbs couldn't quite reach.

{{NAME}} ran the ball to the right, drew three defenders, then used his speed burst at the exact moment he released it: a chip so high it hung in the air for two full seconds.

His teammate with flight caught it and headed it straight down.

The goalkeeper tried. Almost made it.

Two one.

The entity stood at the centre circle for a long moment, then inclined its head: a bow.

pages.content:
Captain Meridian shook his hand on the pitch.

"Reliable," she said, which coming from her was the best compliment he had ever received.

He walked home alone, still in his Flicker suit, his football boots over his shoulder.

In bed that night, he thought about the entity's bow at the end.

Something that could travel between dimensions. Something that played football to settle disputes.

Maybe, he thought, the universe wasn't so different from here.

He closed his eyes, smiling, and fell asleep still thinking about the chip.
